full_text_en:
Jinhong'en Computer Co., Ltd. v. Huiste Technology Development Center — Unfair Competition Dispute

Plaintiff: Beijing Jinhong'en Computer Co., Ltd. Domicile: Pinggu Town, Pinggu County, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Chi Yufeng, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Qu Zhaoxu and Hao Jianping, lawyers from Beijing Lutong Law Firm.

Defendant: Beijing Huiste Technology Development Center. Domicile: Xueyuan South Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Yan Weidong, General Manager of the Company.

The plaintiff, Beijing Jinhong'en Computer Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhong'en Company), filed a lawsuit with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing against the defendant, Beijing Huiste Technology Development Center (hereinafter referred to as Huiste Center), due to a dispute over unfair competition.

Plaintiff's Allegations: In November 1997, the plaintiff independently developed and produced the stock market operation software product "Gu Shen" (Stock God), which was published by Tsinghua University Press. Since its launch, this software has consistently ranked among the top sellers of similar products, occupied a considerable market share, and gained high recognition, becoming a well-known product. On April 28, 1999, the plaintiff obtained Trademark Registration Certificate No. 1268788, enjoying exclusive rights to the "Gu Shen" trademark for goods in Class 9. Starting from 2000, the defendant, Huiste Center, labeled its software product outer packaging with the name "Gu Shen 2000," while the actual software inside was named "Stock Classic." At the same time, Huiste Center, when promoting its developed "Stock Classic" on the company's website homepage, also used words such as "Gu Shen 2000" and "'Gu Shen 2000' grand launch." The above actions of Huiste Center caused consumers to mistakenly believe that "Stock Classic" was an upgraded version of "Gu Shen," infringing upon the plaintiff's legitimate rights and interests. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the court to order Huiste Center to: 1. Immediately stop selling the infringing products, destroy all packaging and decorations of the infringing products, and delete the false promotions on its website homepage; 2. Publicly apologize, eliminate the adverse effects, and publish an apology statement on its website homepage as well as in "China Computer News" and "Computer Business News"; 3. Compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 200,000.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The "Gu Shen" trademark is approved for use on "computer hardware" in Class 9, not including "software." The plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, using the "Gu Shen" trademark on its developed software, is an unauthorized expansion of the trademark's scope of use. In this regard, our center has already filed an application with the State Trademark Office for the cancellation of the improperly registered trademark. 2. "Gu Shen 2000" is an independently developed stock analysis software by our center, and its design and packaging are completely different from Jinhong'en Company's "Gu Shen" software. There is no connection between the two, and it is certainly not an upgraded version of that software. 3. The use of the words "Gu Shen 2000" on our product's outer packaging is because this product is part of the series of another product of our center, "Cai Shen 2000" (Fortune God 2000). The packaging, name, and font of these two software products are consistent and completely different from Jinhong'en Company's "Gu Shen" software. Moreover, it is clearly indicated on the prominent position of the packaging that it is developed by Beijing Huiste Technology Development Center. 4. Jinhong'en Company's claim in the complaint that the "Gu Shen" product is a well-known product is inconsistent with the facts. In terms of product sales volume and market share, Jinhong'en Company is not ranked first, as evidenced by the software distributor sales rankings in Beijing. Based on the above reasons, the court should dismiss all of Jinhong'en Company's claims.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing found the following facts upon trial:

In November 1997, the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, developed the "Gu Shen" software, which was published by Tsinghua University Press. From August to December 1998, Jinhong'en Company placed consecutive advertisements for its products in news media such as "China Computer News," "Workers' Daily," and "China Youth Daily," during which it also promoted the "Gu Shen" software. This software was sold at Beijing Lianbang Software Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lianbang Company) and its chain stores. From December 1997 to September 1999, the "Gu Shen" software was listed among the top sellers for a certain period in the PC software sales category rankings of Lianbang Company.

On April 20, 1999, the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, registered the copyright of the "Gu Shen" software with the National Copyright Administration, with the software abbreviated as "Gu Shen." On April 28, Jinhong'en Company registered the "Gu Shen" trademark with the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Office), with the approved goods listed as Class 9 "computer hardware." On December 28, Jinhong'en Company obtained the "Beijing Software Product Certificate" issued by the Beijing Software Enterprise and Software Product Quality Certification Group, with the product name being "Gu Shen." On April 10, 2000, the Trademark Office accepted Jinhong'en Company's application No. 2000045415, which Jinhong'en Company claimed was to expand the approved scope of use of the "Gu Shen" trademark to "computer software."

On March 27, 2000, the defendant, Huiste Center, filed an application with the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Review Board) to cancel the "Gu Shen" trademark registered by the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, on the grounds of improper registration. On May 12, the Trademark Review Board formally accepted the application, which is still under review. On April 6, 1999, the defendant, Huiste Center, entrusted the publishing of its developed "Stock Classic" analysis system software to the Electronic Industry Press through a publishing contract, with a reproduction quantity of 20,000 discs. Starting from early 2000, Huiste Center began to mark on the outer packaging of the "Stock Classic" software product the words "'Gu Shen 2000' and 'Stock Classic' Millennium Edition," "This software is the second-generation mainstream stock trading software," and placed advertisements in "China Computer News" and "Computer Business News" promoting "Gu Shen 2000." Huiste Center also used "Gu Shen 2000" as a link identifier on the homepage of its company's internet website to promote and sell "Stock Classic." To download the upgraded version of "Stock Classic" software from this website, one needed to click on the "Gu Shen 2000 Upgrade Version" column on the homepage.

The content of the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company's "Gu Shen" software and the defendant, Huiste Center's "Stock Classic" software are different. The fonts used for the word "Gu Shen" by the two parties are also inconsistent, but there is no difference in pronunciation. During the trial, Huiste Center submitted the software ranking list of Lianbang Company to demonstrate the market influence of its "Cai Shen 2000" software.

The plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, submitted the following evidence to the court: 1. One set of "Gu Shen" software; 2. One set of "Gu Shen 2000" software; 3. Two notarized documents; 4. Trademark Registration Certificate No. 1268788; 5. Certificate issued by Lianbang Software Co., Ltd.; 6. Acceptance notice from the Trademark Office; 7. Performance record of "Gu Shen" software; 8. Lianbang PC software sales category rankings; 9. 24 advertisements made by Jinhong'en Company; 10. Product certificate for "Gu Shen" software; 11. Copyright registration certificate for "Gu Shen" software; 12. Invoice for the purchase of "Gu Shen 2000" product; 13. Authorization letter for reproduction of electronic publications, etc. The defendant, Huiste Center, submitted the following evidence: 1. Delivery note from Beijing Trademark Office to the State Administration for Industry and Commerce; 2. Application for cancellation of improperly registered trademark from Beijing Trademark Office; 3. Notice from the Trademark Review Board; 4. Zhengpu software ranking list; 5. Lianbang software ranking list; 6. Outer packaging of "Gu Shen 2000" software; 7. Outer packaging of "Cai Shen 2000" software; 8. Three advertisements of Huiste Center. The above evidence was examined and cross-examined in court and may serve as the basis for determining the facts mentioned above.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing held that:

The plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, enjoys exclusive trademark rights to the "Gu Shen" trademark registered for "computer hardware" in Class 9. Until this exclusive trademark right is cancelled in accordance with legal procedures, it shall be protected by law.

Regarding the scope of exclusive trademark rights, Article 37 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "It shall be limited to the goods approved for use and the trademark approved for registration." Given that the primary function of a trademark is to distinguish the same or similar goods produced or operated by different producers or operators, to prevent confusion of goods and to avoid consumers' misunderstanding of the source or quality of the goods, Article 38(1) of the Trademark Law further stipulates: "Using a trademark that is identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same or similar goods without the permission of the trademark registrant" constitutes an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. This provision prohibits the use of trademarks identical or similar to another's registered trademark on similar goods, thereby extending the protection of exclusive trademark rights to the scope of preventing confusion and misunderstanding of the source and quality of goods. Therefore, what constitutes "similar goods" as referred to in the law must be comprehensively determined based on this legislative purpose, taking into account factors such as product function, material, purpose, and production department.

Computer hardware and computer software are both products closely related to computer operation, belonging to the same major category in the commodity classification table. Using identical or similar trademark marks on computer hardware and software respectively can easily lead consumers to believe that the hardware and software have the same source. Therefore, from the perspective that ordinary consumers are prone to make associative connections, computer hardware and computer software are similar goods as referred to in Article 38(1) of the Trademark Law. The plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, has registered "Gu Shen" as a trademark for "computer hardware." Regardless of whether the company uses the "Gu Shen" trademark on computer software products, others, without the company's permission, must not arbitrarily use trademarks or marks identical or similar to the registered "Gu Shen" trademark on computer software. The defendant, Huiste Center, without the permission of Jinhong'en Company, used marks containing the word "Gu Shen" on computer software. Although the font of the word "Gu Shen" used is inconsistent, there is no difference in pronunciation. When consumers identify the trademark with ordinary attention, they are prone to misidentification. Therefore, such use by Huiste Center constitutes trademark infringement. The protection of trademark rights takes the approved and registered trademark as the object, independent of whether the registrant uses the trademark beyond the scope. Hence, Huiste Center's defense that Jinhong'en Company's use of the registered "Gu Shen" trademark on software products is an unauthorized expansion of the trademark's scope of use, thereby denying its own infringement, is untenable.

Article 5(2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that "using, without authorization, the unique name, packaging, or decoration of a well-known product, or using a name, packaging, or decoration similar to that of another's well-known product, thereby causing confusion with the well-known product of others and leading purchasers to mistakenly believe it is that well-known product," constitutes an act of unfair competition.

The word "Gu Shen" is not a generic name for stock-type software. The plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, named its software "Gu Shen" and launched it on the market prior to the defendant, Huiste Center's "Stock Classic." Jinhong'en Company conducted extensive advertising campaigns to sell the "Gu Shen" software, which led to the software maintaining a leading sales position for a period on the Lianbang professional software ranking list recognized by both parties. Therefore, this software has achieved a certain degree of market recognition in the stock software market and should be recognized as a well-known product.

The naming convention in the software industry is that software copyright holders, when developing upgraded versions, improved versions, or other series products based on their own developed software, generally distinguish them by adding different serial numbers or year numbers after the original name. Starting from 2000, when the defendant, Huiste Center, released the "Stock Classic" Millennium Edition, it printed the words "Gu Shen 2000" and "second-generation mainstream stock trading software" on the outer packaging of the product, and used "Gu Shen 2000" as a link identifier on its website to promote and sell the "Stock Classic" Millennium Edition. This practice, contrary to the industry naming convention, has linked Huiste Center's "Stock Classic" Millennium Edition with the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company's "Gu Shen," sufficiently leading purchasers to mistakenly believe that "Stock Classic" Millennium Edition is an upgraded version of "Gu Shen." Such conduct by Huiste Center has infringed upon Jinhong'en Company's legitimate rights and interests in using its own product name, violating Article 5(2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, constituting unfair competition, and Huiste Center shall bear the legal liability for infringement. Huiste Center's defense, arguing that "Gu Shen 2000" is an independently developed stock analysis software by the center with no connection to Jinhong'en Company's "Gu Shen" software, and that "Gu Shen 2000" is a series product of its "Cai Shen 2000," lacks legal basis; its defense that Jinhong'en Company's "Gu Shen" is not a well-known product and thus Jinhong'en Company does not enjoy the rights of a well-known product lacks factual basis. Therefore, both defenses are untenable.

The defendant, Huiste Center's conduct only involved using the words "Gu Shen 2000" on the software's outer packaging and webpage to promote the "Stock Classic" Millennium Edition, while the software itself still bore the original name "Stock Classic," and the software's content also differs from the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company's "Gu Shen" software. Therefore, Huiste Center's use of the name on the software and the software's content did not infringe upon Jinhong'en Company's legitimate rights and interests. Jinhong'en Company's request for an order that Huiste Center immediately stop selling its products and compensate for losses of RMB 200,000 is inappropriate. The court shall determine the manner of cessation of infringement and the amount of damages based on the degree of infringement by Huiste Center in accordance with the law, and shall not fully support Jinhong'en Company's claims.

In conclusion, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing rendered the following judgment on June 28, 2000:

1. From the effective date of this judgment, the defendant, Huiste Center, shall cease using the word "Gu Shen" on the packaging of its "Stock Classic" software and in related advertising;
2. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, the defendant, Huiste Center, shall publish a statement in "China Computer News" and on its website homepage to publicly apologize to the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company;
3. Within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, the defendant, Huiste Center, shall compensate the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, for economic losses of RMB 20,000. The case acceptance fee of RMB 5,510 shall be borne by the plaintiff, Jinhong'en Company, in the amount of RMB 1,510, and by the defendant, Huiste Center, in the amount of RMB 4,000.

Huiste Center, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, filed an appeal with the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court.

During the second instance trial, both parties expressly stated that they had no objections to the facts found by the court of first instance and also confirmed that Huiste Center's actions constituted infringement. With the mediation conducted by the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement on September 27, 2000:

1. From the date of receipt of this mediation document, Huiste Center shall cease using the word "Gu Shen" on the packaging of its "Stock Classic" software and in related advertising;
2. Huiste Center shall apologize in writing to Jinhong'en Company (already executed);
3. On the date of receipt of this mediation document, Huiste Center shall pay RMB 10,000 to Jinhong'en Company;
4. The case acceptance fee for the first instance of RMB 5,510 shall be borne by Jinhong'en Company; the case acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 5,510 shall be borne by Huiste Center.

This mediation document, upon signature by both parties, has entered into legal force.
